basis: Umbrella of post-bacterial sequelae; no anatomical organ is consistently damaged across its subtypes.
TNNC1-related hypertrophic cardiomyopathy affects cardiac muscle and conduction.
Palmoplantar keratoderma and esophageal disease define the syndrome; hepatomegaly alone does not establish hepatic damage.
Benign adipocytic tumor arising characteristically in subcutaneous tissue.
Skeletal abnormalities, including hallux valgus and cone-shaped epiphyses, occur in 30-79%; obesity and dental abnormalities omitted at the four-axis cap.
Valve disease and intellectual disability define the syndrome; ptosis occurs in 30-79%. Short stature and delayed bone age alone do not establish skeletal damage.
ADCY5-related central movement disorder; orofacial dyskinesia does not establish intrinsic oral or muscular disease.
Localized loss of subcutaneous fat, sometimes with epidermal atrophy; no defining systemic metabolic disorder.
Tumor originates in the epididymis, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss; hearing impairment reported in 13/13 patients.
CNS hypomyelination and neurodegeneration; scoliosis and ptosis in one reported patient do not establish common direct extra-neural injury.
Congenital failure of bone continuity and union in limb bones.
Fibular aplasia and complex brachydactyly are defining skeletal malformations; no supplied evidence supports another axis.
Predisposition to breast and ovarian cancers, both outside the axes; risks of other cancers do not establish organ damage.
Typical 4p deletion phenotype includes neurodevelopmental impairment; skeletal defects ~60%, heart defects ~50%, hearing loss ~40%; deletion extent varies.
Progressive central neurodegeneration causes spastic paraplegia and dementia; dysphagia and weakness are neurologic manifestations.
Inherited hemorrhagic diathesis is a coagulation disorder; no additional organ damage is established.
GPT2 enzyme deficiency disrupts amino-acid metabolism and causes microcephaly, intellectual disability and spastic paraplegia.
Metaphyseal cartilage and bone dysplasia causes short limbs, coxa vara and leg deformity.
Lysosomal storage with neurodevelopmental decline; contractures 2/3 and hearing impairment 1/3; mitral regurgitation 1/3 omitted at the four-axis cap.
Peroxisomal metabolic disease with cortical malformation; hepatic dysfunction is typical, jaundice 1/1; cataract 1/1. Skeletal and renal manifestations omitted by cap.
Congenital hydrocephalus directly affects the brain and ventricular system.
Benign tumor arises in sphenoid sinus respiratory mucosa; paranasal sinuses belong to the pulmonary axis.
Inflammation of the paratenon with degeneration of tendon tissue; no specific autoimmune or infectious mechanism is established.
Inflammation damages ileal pouch mucosa; infection and specific immune-mediated causes are not established across the umbrella condition.
